caption:
do you need sunscreen in the car?

Researchers measured UVA inside 29 cars. Windshields blocked about 96%, and that was almost the same in every car.

Side windows were different: 71% on average, and as low as 44% in some cars. Only 4 of the 29 blocked more than 90% at the side.

On long drives, the side of your face next to the window gets the most.

Send this to the friend with the long commute.

General education only. Not medical advice.

Source:
Boxer Wachler, JAMA Ophthalmol 2016. doi:10.1001/jamaophthalmol.2016.1139
